comparison: Both evaluations find strong support for retinal degeneration claims (C5, C6, C41-C43, C50-C55). OpenEval emphasizes the correlation between recombination efficiency and phenotype severity with statistical analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings, with Reviewer 2 noting 'phenotype severity nicely correlates with the efficiency of Cre-mediated Sox9 depletion.' Both include C44 (Pde6brd1 control), though OpenEval separately evaluates this as UNCERTAIN in R20.

Perfect agreement on claims C56-C60 regarding multiple cell-type marker analysis. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with statistical significance. OpenEval highlights specific p-values (<0.05) for all comparisons. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating the data show 'reduction in the numbers of other retinal cell types such as ganglion cells, amacrine cells and horizontal cells.'

Complete agreement on apoptosis findings (C61-C64). Both evaluations support the TUNEL assay data showing photoreceptor apoptosis. OpenEval notes C64 is speculative regarding temporal dynamics but finds overall conclusions well-supported (p=0.028). Peer reviewers accept these findings without raising concerns, with Reviewer 1 explicitly confirming 'the absence of the ONL is due to apoptosis of photoreceptors.'

Full agreement on reactive gliosis claims (C65-C70). Both evaluations find GFAP immunofluorescence data convincing with statistical significance (p=0.024). OpenEval emphasizes the correlation with phenotype severity. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating 'Müller Glia undergoes reactive gliosis by upregulating the Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein.'

Strong agreement on lineage tracing experiments (C71-C84). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from Sox9-EYFP and Sox9-LacZ reporter data with temporal analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings, with Reviewer 2 praising 'a clever genetic tracing strategy' and confirming 'Sox9 is expressed in a basal limbal stem cell population.' Peer review also includes C7 not in OpenEval R5.

Agreement on scRNA-seq analysis (C85-C97, C126-C127). OpenEval finds strong support from UMAP clustering, pseudotime analysis, and differential gene expression (2816 genes). Peer reviewers confirm the findings, with Reviewer 1 stating the authors 'validate Sox9 expression and characterize its dynamics in limbal stem cells using an existing single-cell RNA sequencing dataset.' Both evaluations accept the interpretation that Sox9-negative cells are more differentiated.

Agreement on mosaic analysis and cell competition model (C98-C108, C131-C133). OpenEval finds support for reduced clonal contribution (p=0.0159) and cell competition model, though notes C106 is speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating 'Sox9 deletion causes progenitor cells to lose their clonogenic capacity' and Reviewer 2 calling the mosaic analysis 'clever.' Peer review also includes C8 not in OpenEval R7.

Both address mechanistic interpretation and main conclusions (C109-C110, C114-C115, C145, C156-C157). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic models are inferential and not definitively established. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with the editor stating 'the data at hand convincingly support the main conclusions.' This represents a key difference: OpenEval is more cautious about mechanistic claims while peer reviewers accept the overall conclusions. Peer review also includes C9-C10 not in OpenEval R8.

Overlap on claims C109-C110 regarding mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval evaluates mechanistic claims as UNCERTAIN. Peer review R9 focuses on novelty of adult-specific approach (C40, C109-C110) and rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 praising the 'inducible genetic approaches in the adult mouse nervous system.' Different emphasis: OpenEval on mechanistic uncertainty, peer review on methodological novelty.

OpenEval evaluates clinical implications (C119-C125) as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are primarily speculative without supporting data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific clinical speculation claims.

OpenEval R10 integrates scRNA-seq trajectory analysis with lineage tracing (C126-C130) and finds support for Sox9 expression decline during differentiation. Peer R6 addresses overlapping scRNA-seq claims (C126-C127) as part of broader molecular characterization. Both find the data convincing, though OpenEval notes some inference about homeostasis mechanism.

OpenEval R11 focuses specifically on cell competition model (C131-C133) based on mosaic analysis and finds it SUPPORTED. Peer R7 addresses these same claims as part of broader mosaic analysis evaluation. Both accept the cell competition explanation for discrepancy between whole-mount and section analysis, though OpenEval notes the mechanism is not directly demonstrated.

OpenEval evaluates concordance/discordance with concurrent work (C134-C136) as UNCERTAIN, noting the explanation for discrepancy is plausible but not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about comparison with other studies.

OpenEval finds support for claims about outer limbus cell behavior (C137-C143) integrating current findings with prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these outer limbus cell claims.

OpenEval R14 evaluates mechanistic interpretation (C144-C151) as UNCERTAIN, noting molecular mechanisms are cited from other studies and not directly demonstrated. Peer R8 includes C145 and rates main conclusions as SUPPORTED. Different granularity: OpenEval distinguishes between well-supported observations and inferential mechanisms, while peer review accepts overall conclusions.

OpenEval finds support for integration of scRNA-seq/lineage tracing with signaling pathway literature (C152-C155), though notes pathway interactions are cited rather than demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these signaling pathway integration claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates main conclusions (C156-C157) as SUPPORTED, finding them well-supported by experimental data. Peer R8 also addresses these main conclusions and rates as SUPPORTED, with the editor affirming 'the data at hand convincingly support the main conclusions.' Strong agreement on overall study conclusions.

OpenEval finds Sox9 expression pattern claims (C1-C4, C24-C26, C45) SUPPORTED based on established literature and current immunofluorescence data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these expression pattern claims, though they are foundational to the study.

OpenEval evaluates anatomical/physiological background claims (C11-C19) as SUPPORTED, noting they represent established knowledge providing necessary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims.

OpenEval R19 evaluates comprehensive literature review (C20-C40) as SUPPORTED, noting C40 correctly identifies the knowledge gap. Peer R9 includes C40 and emphasizes the novelty of the adult-specific approach. Both recognize the study addresses a previously unknown in vivo role, though peer review emphasizes methodological innovation more strongly.

OpenEval evaluates Pde6brd1 control claim (C44) as UNCERTAIN, noting definitive exclusion requires PCR genotyping that was not performed. Peer R1 includes C44 in broader retinal degeneration evaluation rated as SUPPORTED without raising concerns about this control. Different emphasis: OpenEval identifies specific methodological limitation, peer review accepts overall findings.
